title: A dbdatabuild connection file
description: connections/<name>.yaml, a connection/1 file (plan 13, E03). The file name is the connection's name. It holds no address and no login (how the connection is secured is its `tls` block): the login is the environment variable DBDATAKIT_BUILD_<NAME>_READ and _WRITE (the name in capitals, anything but a letter or digit an underscore). The driver is `engine`, `access: readonly` makes the connection only read (never a destination, a tracking connection or a deploy target, and no _WRITE login is read), `dialect` names the SQL dialect (a built-in or one under `dialects:` in dbdatabuild.yml), and the tool's own settings are under `extensions.build`.

schema.description: connection/1, or connection/2 when the file has `grants` (a program that reads only connection/1 then refuses the file by its version).

name.description: The connection's name; equal to the file's name. Letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.

engine.description: The driver, one word. duckdb, odbc and flightsql need `access: readonly`. A connection named after an engine (sqlserver, postgres, fabric) needs no file unless it sets a version or other settings, and then its engine is its name.

dialect.description: The SQL dialect of the system behind the connection, where it is not the driver's own: a built-in (ansi, sqlserver, postgres, fabric, duckdb, mysql, oracle) or a name under `dialects:` in dbdatabuild.yml.

access.description: `readonly`: the tool only reads this connection. The default is `readwrite`.

tls.description: How the connection is secured, applied over whatever the login's string says. The default encrypts and verifies the server's certificate; a development server with a self-signed certificate says `trust_server_certificate: true`, one without encryption `encrypt: false`.

grants.description: Who may use this connection once it is published to a Gateway as a data source (needs `schema: connection/2`): the home groups that may read it, or everyone. They are part of the definition that is published: a publish replaces the Gateway's grants completely, and the Gateway adds none and takes none away. Without grants no home user may use the published data source.

groups.description: Groups of the Gateway's identity home whose members may use the data source (names match ignoring case). Not together with `everyone`.

everyone.description: Every user of the Gateway's identity home may use the data source. Say it deliberately: leaving the groups out opens nothing.

build.description: The tool's own settings for this connection (what `connections.<name>:` held in dbdatabuild.yml before connection files).

version.description: The engine's major version, or the T-SQL level to generate for: 16 for SQL Server 2022 (and a 2025 server at compatibility level 160), 17 for 2025 at level 170. Lets the matrix linter resolve min_version rows.

parameters.description: Values this connection carries, which differ between connections of one application (a store id, a region). Referenced as `${connection.name}`, or `${origin.name}` by a copy that reads from the connection. Names are lowercase words with underscores; values are single values, read as text.

tracking.description: `none` (not tracked, no warning), or another tracking connection (and schema name) for this connection's records.

connection.description: The connection that keeps the records of what the tool built (a connection of this project: its read and write logins are used). Without it, nothing is tracked and every command that would record something warns.

schema.description: The schema name of the tracking tables on that connection. Default: dbdatabuild.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone name (for example `Europe/Berlin`). It decides what `current_date` and `now()` mean in an `expression` resolver of a load on this connection; it wins over the project's. Default: the project's, else UTC. The machine's own zone is never used.

allow_native_commands.description: Whether a native command (a procedure call that returns rows, `kind: {native: {access: command}}`) may be run on this connection. Default false: a procedure can write, so each connection that runs one says so. The read login's permissions are what keep it read-only; the call also runs in a transaction that is rolled back.

max_parallel.description: How many sessions one refresh may have open at this connection at once. At an origin of a copy it counts the sessions that read rows for it (and the checks and `source` resolvers that go with them); at the destination it caps `parallel`, the loads that run together. A limit holds within one run (another process has its own). Default: no limit.

plans.description: This connection's own plan policy; what it leaves out is the project's.

refresh.description: This connection's own refresh check; what it leaves out is the project's.

title.description: A short display name, one line, at most 200 characters. Never inherited.

description.description: Free text, at most 4000 characters. Never inherited.

tags.description: Labels: words of letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.` and `:`, at most 128 characters each.

properties.description: Free key-value data. A value is text, a number or true or false (a number written as plain digits is a number, text in quotes is text); keys are at most 128 characters, values at most 4000.

gateway.description: The Gateway's serving policy for this connection once it is published as a data source (plan 13c D19, owner decision of 2026-11-09): a publish sends it and the Gateway replaces its own with exactly this, no merge. `allow_writes` and `allowed_directories` are not part of a definition and are refused: a publish replaces the whole data source file on the Gateway, so what it publishes is read-only and reads no directories outside its database. Who may use the data source is `grants`, not `groups` or `everyone` here.

pass_through.description: Connect with the caller's own credentials (the database decides who may read).

bitness.description: `x64` (in-process, the default) or `x86` (through the 32-bit worker; ODBC only).

classifier.description: What to do with statement text that is not a single plain SELECT on a read-only data source: `warn`, `strict` (refuse) or `off`.

metadata.description: How catalog metadata is read: `auto`, `odbc` or `informationschema`.

default.description: The data source a home user gets when the client names none (at most one data source of a Gateway).

max_concurrent_queries.description: Most queries running at once on the data source; 0 is no limit.

max_concurrent_queries_per_user.description: Most queries one user may have running at once; 0 is no limit.

acquire_timeout_seconds.description: How long a request waits for a free slot when a limit is set.

compression.description: Overrides the Gateway's compression settings for this data source (the Gateway validates the keys).
